title: Job Asks God for the Charges
overview: Job speaks straight to God, asking why the One who carefully made him now seems set on destroying him without ever saying why.

parts.label: Done holding back (vv. 1-2)
parts.note: Job is so worn out by his suffering that he decides to say exactly what he feels. He asks God not to treat him as guilty without first telling him what he is accused of.

parts.label: Are you like a human judge? (vv. 3-7)
parts.note: Job asks whether it pleases God to crush what his own hands made while the wicked seem to prosper. He asks if God sees as narrowly as a person does, or has so little time that he must hunt for faults, when Job believes God already knows he is not guilty and no one can rescue him.

parts.label: You made me so carefully (vv. 8-12)
parts.note: Job pictures God shaping him like a potter with clay, and forming him in the womb like milk thickening into cheese, an ancient way of imagining how a body takes shape. He sets that careful, kind making against the ruin he is living through now.

parts.label: Was this the plan all along? (vv. 13-17)
parts.note: Job fears God was secretly watching all along, waiting to punish, so that guilty or innocent he cannot win. He feels hunted like prey by a lion, with fresh troubles arriving one after another like new witnesses against him or waves of troops.

parts.label: Why was I ever born? (vv. 18-22)
parts.note: Job repeats his wish that he had died at birth and begs God to leave him alone for a little relief before he dies. He pictures the world of the dead as a land of total darkness and disorder, where even the light is dark.

disagreement: Christians differ on whether Job's bitter words here are faithless complaint he later has to take back, or honest grief that God accepts, since God later says Job spoke rightly about him (Job 42:7).
think: When something painful happens with no explanation, what feels more honest to you: protesting out loud, staying quiet, or something else?
